humanQuestions.decision: (1)(a), (2)(a), (3)(a) — owner reply https://github.com/myungjoo/HIL-Claw/issues/5#issuecomment-6052377983: the reference is NumPy float64 (the float64 product of the drawn fp32 inputs widened to float64), computed on the Python side of the harness; the process that runs the kernel holds neither the reference nor the comparison; `numpy` becomes the first runtime dependency of `hilclaw`, approved by this answer, pinned exactly by the code task that adds it (newest release with wheels for CPython 3.11 and 3.14); how inputs and the kernel's output reach the Python side is the record's design and is not decided; this closes the "Still open" line of A-7 for `cpu_standin` only, not B-7 in general. Tolerance: per-element `rtol` and `atol`, both instance parameters (FR-9); pass iff |out - ref| <= atol + rtol*|ref| for every element; any NaN or infinity in the output fails; premise: the verification inputs of this case are drawn finite. Defaults: none, an instance must state both; StandardScenarios S0 step 2 is reworded in the coverage re-check of T-0036. Note: read ADR-0010 to ADR-0016 as well, ADR-0016 in particular, and re-read the scope sentence "not an FR-10 tool contract" against it; the answer does not decide the harness/backend split.
